key_insight: The paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical detector for affinity and romance-investment fraud that encodes cognitive manipulation patterns in qubits and uses reinforcement learning to decide when to flag a conversation.
engineering_relevance: It suggests a structured quantum representation for sequential fraud cues, combined with an optimal-stopping RL policy for turn-by-turn intervention in conversational security systems.
method: Dedicated qubits encode key cognitive biases involved in manipulation.
A frame qubit captures temporal order of reframing; a narrative qubit aggregates co-occurrence via trainable entanglement.
A classical RL agent jointly trains with the quantum circuit to decide whether to flag the conversation at each turn.
evidence_signal: The model is evaluated on synthetic conversations, including hard negatives and legitimate urgent or pushy sales scenarios.
watch_item: Results are based on synthetic data, so real-world robustness and transfer to live conversational fraud remain unproven.
paper_title: A Cognitive-Aware QML-CRL Framework for Detecting Affinity and Romance-Investment Fraud
